memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the Lord your God has destroyed the nations whose land he is giving you, and when you have driven them out and settled in their towns and houses, then set aside for yourselves three cities in the land the Lord your God is giving you to possess. - Deut 19:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel prepared to settle in the land, God gave a thoughtful command, set aside three cities. These were not ordinary towns. They were to be cities of refuge, places where a person who had accidentally killed someone could flee for safety before the matter was properly judged. Even before His people faced such situations, God was making merciful provision for them.

Think about the heart of God shown here. He was not only concerned with land, borders, and victory. He was concerned with justice tempered by mercy, with protecting the vulnerable from hasty revenge. In a world quick to shed blood, God built havens of safety into the very map of the land.

This tender care points us toward something greater. We too need a refuge, not from an avenger of blood, but from the guilt and consequences of our sin. God has provided that refuge in Christ. In Him we find shelter, safety, and mercy that we could never earn. Scripture speaks of fleeing to take hold of the hope set before us, a hope that is a secure anchor for the soul (Heb 6:18-19). God still delights to be a refuge for His people. When you feel exposed and afraid, do you know where to run? Have you found your true refuge in Christ, the safe place God Himself has provided?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you run when life feels overwhelming?
2. What does it mean that God provides a refuge for you?
3. How is Christ your ultimate place of safety?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for being a refuge for Your people. When I am afraid and exposed, help me run to Christ, my safe and sure shelter. Amen.
